Busy for a reason, and the fish curry was the star
Sep 2026 • Couples
We walked past Tandoor several times and it was busy every time. To me that's the best sign a restaurant is good. The other sign was the number of Indian travelers eating there. We met a large group from Mumbai, and they had very good things to say about the food.

The restaurant was super clean, and the food arrived hot and quick. That says everything.

I was hesitant about Indian food in Vietnam, but then I thought about how fresh the seafood is here and figured it would make a perfect fish curry. We ordered chili prawns, fish vindaloo, chicken curry with rice, and naan. The fish curry was the star. The fish tasted fresh, and the sauce was bold and well-spiced without drowning it.

If you're looking for a good seafood curry and chili prawns, I highly recommend Tandoor.

Tip: order extra. The leftovers were even better after a night out clubbing.

Excellent Indian food... in HCMC?!
Dec 2025 • Solo
Loved this place. Flat out.

The garlic naan was outstanding — hot, soft, properly garlicky, and done exactly right. Lamb samosas were excellent, crisp outside, rich and flavorful inside. And the chicken tikka masala? Fantastic. Rich, well-spiced, and nailed. Exactly what you want. Tikka Masala dancing in my head. 

Service was attentive.

Only small nit: the tikka masala comes in a bowl not over rice. You have to order the rice separately, then pour it over yourself. Easy enough, just worth knowing.

All in, a really great dinner. I’ll be back.

Disrespectful towards Hindus
Nov 2025 • Solo
Apart from average food and attentive staff, major concern on which I'd like to draw attention of the owners of this restaurant. 

They have put a Shivalinga on the entrance (as soon as you enter at the restaurant) and also using Jaldhari on it filled with water. This restaurant is offering non veg and making fun of Hindus sentiment. They have many Indian staff including Indian restaurant manager but I'm surprised why no one ever took a corrective measurement

Shivlinga is not for decoration, must not be put as a decorative item inside a restaurant, at the entrance exactly and where non veg is veing served. 

I wish they understand this and respect the Indian culture and religious sentiments. I dare them to put a funny cartoon of Allah and see the reaction of Muslim visitors at their restaurant.
